solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Chatted desultorily about soldiers in unit

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the soldiers, so they surround that piece
done in a random, aimless way, so the letters of the first word are jumbled

parts.note: men is the usual crossword word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops in a military unit idly chatting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desultorily' (aimlessly) signals the jumble, and 'about' wraps the jumble around the soldiers; men is the standard word for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a body of troops sent off on a separate task, so a military unit.

clue.text: Losing feathers

definitions.meaning: behind in a game or contest, trailing the opponent by some points
the fine soft plumage of young birds, used to fill pillows

explanation.surface: A bird moulting, losing its plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a team trailing is a goal behind, and soft fluffy plumage is a filling for duvets.

clue.text: Speculates gold is found in working these

indicators.note: the gold and is are placed inside the rearranged letters
the word these is set to work, i.e. its letters are rearranged

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miner guessing whether gold will turn up in these workings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' signals the jumble and 'found in' the insertion; OR as gold comes from heraldry and French.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form ideas or conjectures, which is what someone who speculates does.

clue.text: Sees what's worth stealing from containers

definitions.meaning: a burglar reconnoitring a place, as in the phrase to case the joint
boxes or holders, such as suitcases or display boxes

explanation.surface: A thief eyeing what is worth taking out of some boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who scouts a target beforehand 'cases' it, and boxes or holders are also known by the same plural noun.

clue.text: Thinking about making a hot drink?

definitions.meaning: pondering or turning something over in the mind
warming wine or ale with spices and sugar, as with Christmas punch

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether to brew something warm.
explanation.definitionFit: To mull over is to ponder, and mulled wine is heated with spices, so both senses share the verb.

clue.text: Plants bananas Maggie imported

indicators.note: brought into, so one name sits inside the other word

parts.note: slang for crazy, the same as nuts
Meg is a short form of Margaret, like Maggie

explanation.surface: Maggie has been bringing in banana plants from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but is slang for crazy; 'imported' signals one piece going inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is an evergreen tree whose seed is the spice, so the plural names plants.

clue.text: Bit a hole in it beforehand

indicators.note: the word it, with the hole inside, comes before the letter a
the hole is placed within the next word

parts.note: taken as written
O is the shape of a hole

explanation.surface: Someone biting a hole in something in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' looks like the past tense of bite; it is the noun for a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter is a byword for the smallest amount, as in not one jot.

clue.text: Not bad? A very good animal

parts.note: OK means acceptable, all right
PI is short for pious, very good in a sanctimonious way

explanation.surface: Asking whether an animal is not bad or actually very good.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, for pious, is a crossword convention for 'very good' or holy.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African mammal related to the giraffe, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Quite a number got upset by anaesthetic

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word got is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A patient left quite upset by the anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals the turnaround of a short word; 'Quite a number' looks like one phrase but splits after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means entirely or completely, a synonym of quite in the sense of wholly.

clue.text: Laments few words at end of letter

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small or little, so a wee few
a postscript, abbreviated PS, is added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A letter-writer adding a few sad words in a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to cry, and crying is how one laments, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: What grandma made, to acquire newest skill?

parts.note: the latest thing is the most recent or newest
art means a skill or knack, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Grandma taking up the newest skill in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who begins something only in later life has made a tardy beginning, as a grandmother learning computing would.

clue.text: Good heavens! A marble statue of myself!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, a British expression of astonishment
read literally: turn me into rock

explanation.surface: Someone astonished to find a marble statue of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The British exclamation of surprise is literally a request to turn the speaker into rock, as a marble statue would.

clue.text: Peters out when one goes in for break

indicators.note: the one is placed inside the rearranged letters
out signals the letters of Peters are put out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Peters leaving while another takes his place for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the jumble and 'goes in' the insertion; Peters looks like a name but is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or pause from effort, so a break.

clue.text: With no score, footballer is unsettled

parts.note: a score of nil is written as O, zero
a wing is a footballer who plays out wide

explanation.surface: A goalless winger feeling restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' looks like restless; it means not yet paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill still due is unpaid, and an unpaid debt is one not yet settled.

clue.text: Photograph dressed as a woman that's seen in bed?

parts.note: a snap is a casual photograph
a man with drag on is wearing women's clothes

explanation.surface: A photo of a man in women's clothing turning up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not one for sleeping in.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden flower grown in beds, so something seen in a flower bed.

clue.text: Retiring, procures information about pension fund

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
the information word goes around the procures word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
gets means obtains or procures

explanation.surface: A retiree gathering details about a pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets one piece around the other, then 'Retiring' turns the whole assembly backwards; gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings put aside for later life, such as a pension pot, are a reserve kept for the future.

clue.text: Feeling there's a string attached to proposal

parts.note: E is a violin or guitar string
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A proposal that comes with strings attached.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the name of a string on a violin or guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling such as joy or anger is a state of mind, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Trick is to make little sound

indicators.note: make sound means what is heard rather than what is written

parts.note: slight means small or little

explanation.surface: A trick that consists of making very little noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like noise; it signals a word said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is a conjuring trick, so the word on its own names deft deception.

clue.text: Animal crate assembled and put in warm covering

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the animal

parts.note: a goat is an animal

indicators.note: put together in a new way, so the crate letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal crate being put together and lined with something warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' signals the jumble and 'put in' the insertion; 'Animal' looks like a description of the crate but supplies a piece itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat, a warm garment that covers the body.

clue.text: They shoot back after opening to have a drink

indicators.note: back means read in reverse, so everything that follows is turned around
the drink comes after the opening

parts.note: a slot is a narrow opening
to sip is to drink a little

explanation.surface: Gunmen returning after the bar opens to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOT then SIP read 'back' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Handguns are weapons that shoot, so they fit the description.

clue.text: RAF ace?

definitions.meaning: the Royal Air Force is one of the armed forces
in tennis, an ace is a serve the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: Looks like a fighter pilot of the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: The RAF is one of the armed forces, and a tennis ace is a winning serve: both are examples.

clue.text: Go ahead and quietly hand over again

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to re-cede is to cede, or surrender, a second time

explanation.surface: Telling someone to proceed and discreetly pass something back.
explanation.walkthrough: RE-CEDE splits as cede once more, not recede meaning withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: To come before something is to go ahead of it in time or order.

clue.text: If you don't mind being very old-fashioned

definitions.text: If you don't mind being very old-fashioned

parts.words: If you don't mind being very old-fashioned
parts.note: a polite request, as in please, expressed in a long-obsolete way

explanation.surface: Asking someone to tolerate being terribly old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word is a contraction of 'I pray thee', an antiquated way of saying please.

clue.text: Master with pet whose tail has been docked

indicators.note: docking cuts off the tail, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a rabbit is a common pet

explanation.surface: A teacher with a pet whose tail has been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher, and the word literally means master or my teacher.

clue.text: Complain of regrettable error in closing section

indicators.note: error signals the extracted letters are wrongly arranged
only the closing section of the word regrettable is used, its opening letters dropped

explanation.surface: Grumbling about an unfortunate mistake at the end of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing section' keeps the end of 'regrettable', giving TABLE, and 'error' scrambles that; 'error' reads as a noun in the surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to whine or moan feebly, like a sheep, so to complain.

clue.text: In Gap, design clothes

indicators.note: the design word goes inside the gap word

parts.note: a rent is a tear or gap
an aim is an intention or design

explanation.surface: Designing clothes for the Gap fashion chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gap' looks like the clothing retailer; it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Algerian? Wrong. Scotsman? No. Englishman? Famously

indicators.note: wrong signals the remaining letters of Algerian are rearranged
no signals the Scotsman is removed from the letters of Algerian

parts.note: Ian is the stereotypical Scottish man's name in crosswords

explanation.surface: A quiz about nationality: not Algerian, not Scottish, but famously English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes IAN from ALGERIAN, and 'Wrong' scrambles the ALGER left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward, composer of the Enigma Variations, is a celebrated English composer.

clue.text: Buck up with that pipe

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a buck is a male deer

explanation.surface: Cheer up with a pipe to smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck up' looks like 'cheer up'; buck is the male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe or musical tube can be made from a hollow plant stem, and that stem is also the word for a woodwind mouthpiece.

clue.text: Excited cheering as point is secured by Arsenal's neighbour

indicators.note: the point is held within the scrambled letters
excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: W, for West, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Football fans cheering as their team grabs a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal looks like the football club; it is the old Royal Arsenal at Woolwich, a district of south-east London next door.
explanation.definitionFit: The London borough beside Woolwich, home of the Royal Arsenal, is its neighbour.

clue.text: Bird goes off without egg

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters go around the egg
off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A bird leaving its nest without laying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmyard waterfowl, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Reading back letters 5-14 or one of A-G?

indicators.note: reading in reverse means the letters are taken from right to left

parts.note: the fifth letter of the alphabet is E and the fourteenth is N, so this reads as E to N

explanation.surface: A question about which letters to read, or a musical one.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 5-14 of the alphabet are 'E to N', ETON, which reversed is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical pitches are named with the letters A to G, so each is one example.

clue.text: Got through prison, badly treated

parts.note: pen is US slang for a penitentiary

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of treated are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A prisoner who was badly treated while doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something is to pass right into or through it.
